areas.name: Russian-occupied Ukraine
areas.note: Crimea (occupied since 2014) and the parts of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Kharkiv and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts held since 2022: about a fifth of Ukraine. Russia claims to have annexed Crimea and four oblasts. Drawn as the Ukrainian municipalities (OpenStreetMap level 3, via geoBoundaries) that are mostly occupied on DeepStateMap's map, so the line is approximate at the scale of individual municipalities.

areas.name: West Bank and East Jerusalem
areas.note: Under Israeli military occupation since 1967; East Jerusalem was annexed by Israel. The Palestinian Authority administers civil affairs in Areas A and B (about 40% of the West Bank).

sources.title: Natural Earth 1:10m Admin 0 disputed areas (v5.1.1)

areas.name: Israeli-held Gaza
areas.note: East of the 'yellow line' set by the October 2025 ceasefire, which Israel has since pushed westward: Israeli estimates put its share of the Strip at about 63% in October 2026.

areas.name: Hamas-held Gaza
areas.note: West of the yellow line: Gaza City's western neighborhoods, the central camps, and western Khan Younis and al-Mawasi. Hand-drawn approximation of a line that moves.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Yellow Line (Gaza)

areas.name: Golan Heights
areas.note: Held by Israel since 1967 and annexed in 1981; the United States recognized the annexation in 2019, but nearly all other states consider it occupied Syrian territory. Includes the Shebaa Farms, claimed by Lebanon.

sources.title: Natural Earth 1:10m Admin 0 disputed areas (v5.1.1)

areas.name: Syrian buffer zone and Mount Hermon
areas.note: Israeli forces entered the UN-patrolled buffer zone after Assad's fall in December 2024 and said they would stay; I couldn't confirm their 2026 positions.

sources.title: AAP: Israeli troops to stay in buffer zone inside Syria

areas.name: Suwayda
areas.note: Run by Druze factions under a single National Guard aligned with Sheikh al-Hijri since the July 2025 massacres; the government still holds the province's western and far eastern edges.

sources.title: Syria Direct: Suwayda stands at a crossroads
UN Syria Commission report on Suwayda (March 2026)

areas.name: Houthi-held Yemen
areas.note: The north and west, home to most of Yemen's population. Drawn at the district level; the front has barely moved since the April 2022 truce. After the separatist STC's December 2025 offensive collapsed and the group dissolved in January 2026, the south is held by government and Saudi-backed forces.

sources.title: MERIP: Yemen After the Saudi-Emirati Split (July 2026)
Middle East Institute: Riyadh takes the helm in Yemen
Wikipedia: 2025-2026 southern Yemen campaign

areas.name: Eastern and southern Libya
areas.note: Held by Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army, with the parallel House of Representatives government; the lines have been stable since the 2020 ceasefire, with Turkish forces in the west and Russian ones in Haftar's territory deterring either side.

sources.title: NYRB: Libya, the Dangerous Gamble (August 2026)
Kuwait Times: Libyan National Army conducts grand exercises

areas.name: RSF-held Sudan
areas.note: Almost all of Darfur, where El Fasher fell in October 2025, and nearly all of West Kordofan, where Babanusa's army base fell in December 2025.

areas.name: Jebel Marra and Tawila
areas.note: The SLM faction of Abdel Wahid al-Nur holds parts of these localities, outside both army and RSF control.

sources.title: Sudans Post: Territorial control map as of 25 September 2026

areas.name: Nuba Mountains and southern Blue Nile
areas.note: SPLM-North (al-Hilu) has held the core of the Nuba Mountains since 2011 and, with the RSF, parts of southern Blue Nile. Kadugli and Dilling remain army-held under siege.

areas.name: North Kordofan front
areas.note: Bara has changed hands repeatedly; the army took Sodari on 25 September and says it took al-Mazroub in early October.

areas.note: Claimed by both Sudan and South Sudan and patrolled by UN peacekeepers (UNISFA) since 2011.

areas.name: AFC/M23-held Kivu
areas.note: Goma (January 2025), Bukavu (February 2025) and the surrounding territories. Peace talks under the Doha framework agreed a roadmap in August 2026, but fighting continues.

areas.note: Contested between AFC/M23 and the army and its allies; positions change hands week to week.

areas.name: Puntland
areas.note: Has governed itself without recognizing the federal government since 2024, pending constitutional changes; it is fighting Islamic State in the Cal Miskaad mountains.

areas.name: Sool and Buhodle (SSC-Khatumo)
areas.note: Taken from Somaliland by SSC-Khatumo forces in 2023; now a federal member state (North Eastern State) aligned with Mogadishu. Somaliland still claims it.

areas.name: Jubaland
areas.note: Holds Kismayo and the Lower Juba towns; broke with the federal government after its contested 2024 election and repelled federal forces.

areas.name: Middle Juba
areas.note: Al-Shabaab's heartland, held for the group's entire existence; it also controls much of rural southern and central Somalia (see the insurgent-presence layer).
